messages:
Alex: Heads up — customer reported repeated SSE disconnects and lots of partial events after today's runtime deploy. High reconnect rate + billing spike. Logs show repeated 'write error: EAGAIN' then 'connection aborted'. Can reproduce intermittently.

Maria: Can you paste the exact log lines and which model/route?

Alex: Sure, example from proxy.log: 
```
2024-10-12T15:02:31Z INFO conn=abcd1234 write error: EAGAIN (sendq=65536)
2024-10-12T15:02:31Z WARN conn=abcd1234 aborting connection after write failure
2024-10-12T15:02:31Z INFO conn=abcd45 client reconnect, last_event_id=4321
```
Route: /v1/stream/generate, model: open-llama-13b, streaming enabled.

Sanjay: Looks like the send queue is filling because the client is reading slowly. Can you run `ss -tn src` or `netstat -anp | grep <pid>` while reproducing? Also grab /proc/net/sockstat and the socket sendq numbers.

Alex: Ran `ss -tnp` during repro, snippet: 
```
ESTAB 0 65536 10.0.1.23:443 10.2.8.11:52344 users:("redwood-proxy",pid=2345,fd=42)
```
send-q is pegged at 65536 on several connections.

Jen Ops: That 65536 looks like the kernel send buffer limit. If the client isn't ACKing, the kernel buffers fill and the runtime hits our internal write threshold and aborts to protect memory. Short-term mitigation: increase SO_SNDBUF and reduce server-side batching.

Maria: We pushed a quick config change to lower streaming batch_size from 32 -> 8 for the affected route and enabled `flush_every_event: true` in streaming options. Customer reported fewer aborts in the short window.

Sanjay: Repro steps I used locally: slow-reader Node script below — it intentionally reads the SSE stream with a delay to simulate a mobile client.
```js
const EventSource = require('eventsource');
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream/generate');
es.onmessage = (m) => {
  // slow consumer: process each message with 2s delay
  setTimeout(() => console.log('event', m.data), 2000);
};
```
Triggering that against prod-like load reproduces EAGAIN within ~30s.

Alex: Can we avoid aborting so aggressively? Customer is losing partial outputs (they store partials) and we're billing them for reconnect churn. Suggest changing abort policy to backoff and allow limited queued tokens before abort.

Sanjay: Agreed. Eng-runtime has an abort threshold (WRITE_QUEUE_LIMIT) that is static. I'll propose a patch: make it adaptive based on p99 client ack latency and per-connection memory cap. Also add a metric `conn_sendq_bytes` so we can trigger alerts before aborts.

support-bot: Ticket ENG-1234 created and assigned to @Sanjay. Priority: P1 (customer impact).

Jen Ops: Temporary prod tweak applied in region us-east-1: increased SO_SNDBUF to 262144 and lowered default batch_size for streaming routes. Watching metrics now. :thumbsup:

Sanjay: I'll open a PR for the adaptive threshold and add a runtime flag to disable immediate abort (default off). ETA: EOD for PR + test, rollout early next week.

Alex: Thanks — please confirm once PR merges so we can inform customer and billing about reduced churn. Also want a short runbook for support: steps to mitigate (lower batch, increase sndbuf, enable flush_every_event).

Maria: Will write the runbook and include the repro script + ss/netstat commands. I'll also add note for billing to suppress duplicate invoices if reconnects are within 5m window.

Sanjay: Follow-up will include dashboards: conn_sendq_bytes, streaming_batch_size, per-route aborts. I'll post links when ready.

Alex: Great, closing the slack thread once PR and runbook are done. Thanks team!
